- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.6), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% of recent range.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots downward in next 5–7 days; apply a 1–3% upward bias to offset lag.
- If sentiment is positive and price is falling, model underreacts; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to prevent premature mean reversion.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; add 0.5–1.5% to first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed, model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before applying correction.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion after a spike, model often fails to recognize it; apply 1–2% downward bias in 10–15 day horizon if sentiment is weak or negative.
